_meta.source: Authored for this app. Institutional specifics follow data/pathways.json; support schemes named (bursaries, WSG, e2i, SkillsFuture, AIC) are real and current as of 2026-08-05; every private person, firm and stall is invented.
_meta.notes: The deck contract, enforced by the sweep and the lint: two or three responses each; any response with needsAsk carries a stretch; setbacks carry onward moves with amounts and offices; every requiresFlag names a real flag and every flag is read somewhere; NS cards gate on the run's answer, never on the player; at most 30 percent of outcomes open with You; no first clause repeats; one aphorism per string; dialogue is allowed and quoted.

cards.title: The form comes home
cards.body: Subject combination form, due Friday. Everyone at the table has an opinion and most of them left school before Full SBB existed.

responses.label: Walk them through it
responses.outcome: Auntie included, you explain G2 and G3 with the booklet open. The table calms once the padlocks turn out to be imaginary.

responses.label: Decide first, then tell
responses.outcome: The form goes in with your handwriting on it. Dinner is quieter for a week, then your results start speaking for you.
responses.stretch: It comes out shaky: half your reasons are borrowed. Saying them aloud anyway is how they become yours.

responses.label: Let them decide
responses.outcome: Pa picks what his boss's daughter took. The year teaches you which subjects fit and which were borrowed clothes.

cards.title: Your sibling's shadow
cards.body: The Science teacher taught your brother. First practical, she hands back your worksheet: not bad, but your brother would have finished question five.

responses.label: Outwork the comparison
responses.outcome: By June the worksheets come back with your own name in the margin comments. The shadow shrinks to sibling size.

responses.label: Name it, politely
responses.outcome: I am not him, you say, after class, heart hammering. She blinks, apologises, and starts seeing you.
responses.stretch: It comes out blunter than planned and she stiffens. The apology arrives a week later, and so does the seeing.

responses.label: Let it slide
responses.outcome: The comparison fades on its own by Sec 3. Some fights resolve by outlasting them.

cards.title: The reclass
cards.body: Sec 3 reshuffles everyone by combination. Your lunch table of three years is now split across four classrooms and two recess slots.

responses.label: Keep the old table
responses.outcome: Friday bubble tea at the interchange becomes the standing order. Different classes, same people, on purpose.

responses.label: Build the new one
responses.outcome: The girl beside you in the new class becomes the friend you did not know you were missing.

onwardMoves: A standing weekly meetup keeps old friends without costing new ones.
Two terms is roughly what a new class takes to feel like yours.

cards.title: Open house Saturday
cards.body: Ngee Ann and ITE College Central run open houses the same Saturday your CCA wants you at training. Kakis are going without you if you skip.

responses.label: Go and ask real questions
responses.outcome: A second year student answers what the brochure would not: workload, money, which lecturers to chase. Your shortlist rewrites itself.

responses.label: Send questions with a friend
responses.outcome: Your kaki returns with photos and half answers. Better than nothing, thinner than being there.

responses.label: Train instead
responses.outcome: The competition is in three weeks and the open house is annual. Fair trade, this once.

cards.title: The nationals call
cards.body: Your teacher forwards a form: national competition, your category, submissions due in five weeks. The last school winner got their photo in the foyer.

responses.label: Enter, all in
responses.outcome: Five weekends vanish into the entry. It places nowhere, and the judge's feedback sheet teaches you more than the term did.
responses.stretch: Halfway in you want to quit; finishing badly still beats the version where you never find out.

responses.label: Enter something small
responses.outcome: The junior category, the safer piece. It wins a merit, which whispers instead of shouting.

responses.label: Not this year
responses.outcome: The form expires quietly. Next year's version finds you readier.

cards.title: The Mother Tongue wall
cards.body: Everything else moves except Mother Tongue. Thursday tuition at the CC eats the evening, and the aunty teacher keeps saying the same thing: read aloud more.

responses.label: Do the boring thing daily
responses.outcome: Ten minutes of reading aloud at the kopitiam table, every day, for a term. The grade shifts one band and stays.

responses.label: Ask about your real options
responses.outcome: Your teacher maps it honestly: what B3 unlocks, what MTL B means, what a retake costs. The wall becomes a door with steps.

responses.label: Park it, protect the rest
responses.outcome: You hold MTL steady and pour the hours where they pay. A ceiling on one subject is not a ceiling on you.

onwardMoves: MTL B exists for students the language is genuinely heavy for. Ask your school.
A retake in November is normal and thousands do it each year.

cards.title: The quiet arithmetic
cards.body: The class chalet is forty dollars. You hear your parents in the kitchen doing the end of month maths, and you fold the consent form into your pocket.

responses.label: Ask the form teacher quietly
responses.outcome: There is quite a lot, asked quietly: the school fund covers trips, EZ Link top ups, meals. Nobody makes it a thing.

responses.label: Earn it yourself
responses.outcome: Three weekends of flyer distribution at Tampines Hub covers the chalet and a little pride. Tiring, and entirely yours.

responses.label: Skip the chalet
responses.outcome: The photos sting for a weekend. The friendships survive a missed barbecue comfortably.

onwardMoves: Every school has a student welfare fund and the form teacher holds the key.
Edusave sits in your name already; awards top it up yearly.

cards.title: The group chat goes bad
cards.body: A joke you sent gets screenshot and reread without its tone. By Monday two tables are not talking to you and one is talking about you.

responses.label: Apologise in person
responses.outcome: Face to face at the canteen, no audience. It is wobbly and it works; the screenshot loses its power by Friday.
responses.stretch: The words come out wrong the first time. The second try lands, and trying twice is what gets remembered.

responses.label: Wait it out
responses.outcome: Drama has a half life of roughly two weeks. It passes, and leaves a small scar where a sorry would have been.

onwardMoves: An apology without an audience fixes most of what a group chat breaks.
The school counsellor has seen every version of this and keeps confidences.

cards.title: The reunion dinner audit
cards.body: Second aunt, halfway through the pen cai: so which class are you in now? Express or Normal? The table goes helpfully quiet for your answer.

responses.label: Explain the new system
responses.outcome: There are no streams anymore, auntie, you say, and walk her through G3 Geography beside G2 Maths. Grudging nods around the lazy susan.

responses.label: Give the short version
responses.outcome: Doing fine, auntie. More pen cai? The interrogation moves to your cousin's ang pow job.

responses.label: Quote your plan
responses.outcome: You name the course you are aiming for and the road to it. Second aunt, disarmed, offers her colleague's number.
responses.stretch: Naming a plan you are not sure of feels like borrowing clothes. Saying it aloud starts the fitting.

cards.title: Mid year, she leaves
cards.body: The one teacher who made the subject make sense is posted out in June. The replacement teaches from the slides, at slide speed.

responses.label: Learn to self serve
responses.outcome: Past papers, one good YouTube channel, a study group of three. The subject survives the handover because you carried it.

responses.label: Write to her anyway
responses.outcome: Teachers answer emails from students who cared. Two replies from her new school untangle the whole July topic.

responses.label: Drift a term
responses.outcome: The grade dips one band before you catch it. Some lessons arrive as invoices.

onwardMoves: Your year head can pair you with the department's other strong teacher.
A three person study group replaces about half of a good teacher.

cards.title: It goes wrong publicly
cards.body: The solo, the penalty, the debate rebuttal: yours, and it fails in front of everyone with phones. Someone claps kindly, which is worse.

responses.label: Show up next week
responses.outcome: Training resumes Tuesday and you are there, on time, ears hot. The flop shrinks into the anecdote it deserved to be.

responses.label: Debrief it with the coach
responses.outcome: The coach rewinds it kindly: preparation, not talent, failed you. The fix list is short and concrete.

responses.label: Quit the exposed spot
responses.outcome: The second row suits you for a season. Some retreats are rest, not surrender.

onwardMoves: A coach debrief inside a week turns a flop into technique.
Nobody's highlight reel includes the term they sat out.

cards.title: The transfer student
cards.body: New kid arrives in March from another school, accent from somewhere else, eating alone by the drinks stall on day three.

responses.label: Take your tray over
responses.outcome: Turns out he mods games and his mum makes epok epok for the block. Your circle grows one permanent member.

responses.label: Wave him into the project
responses.outcome: The group needed a fourth anyway. Competence arrives wearing an unfamiliar uniform.

responses.label: Keep your lane
responses.outcome: Someone else takes the tray over. The kindness happened; it just was not yours this time.

cards.title: The corner office nobody visits
cards.body: The ECG counsellor's room, next to the bookshop, is empty most lunches. The poster outside says ask me about anything after Sec 4. Nobody does.

responses.label: Book the slot
responses.outcome: Forty minutes with the pathways map spread on the table. She draws your three options with actual numbers on the arrows.

responses.label: Send your question by email
responses.outcome: The reply comes with two links and an offer to talk. Half the value, none of the nerves.

responses.label: Figure it out yourself
responses.outcome: The MOE website at midnight answers some of it. The room with the actual human stays unvisited.

cards.title: The first real F
cards.body: A module, a crit, a supplementary paper: your first adult sized fail, with your name printed next to it. Nobody phones your parents. That part is on you now.

responses.label: Read the feedback twice
responses.outcome: Under the grade sits a paragraph that is actually a map. The retake passes with room to spare.

responses.label: Tell someone same day
responses.outcome: Saying it out loud to your mother deflates it from disaster to event. She had two of these herself, it turns out.

responses.label: Hide it a month
responses.outcome: The resit fee doubles for late sign up. Silence, it turns out, has an admin charge.

onwardMoves: Every institution runs supplementary assessments; the deadline is the only trap.
One F in a transcript of thirty modules reads as a story, not a verdict.

cards.title: The month the maths breaks
cards.body: Textbook, materials fee, transport, and your phone screen cracks in the same fortnight. The number in the banking app goes red before the fifteenth.

responses.label: Take the campus job
responses.outcome: Library desk, ten hours a week, between classes. The maths mends and the timetable tightens like a drum.

responses.label: Apply for the bursary
responses.outcome: The financial aid office processes it without drama: books covered, one semester's breathing room. Forms, not shame.

responses.label: Freelance the gap
responses.outcome: Two weekend gigs cover the screen. Feast and famine, but the famine ends.

onwardMoves: Bursaries at poly, ITE and uni cover far more students than apply.
Campus jobs schedule around exams because campuses invented exams.

cards.title: The one who tells you things
cards.body: The senior tech, the studio manager, the tutor on contract: one of them starts telling you things nobody writes down. Which clients pay late. Which cert actually matters.

responses.label: Ask for the next layer
responses.outcome: How did you get here, you ask. The whole map comes out over teh at the void deck coffeeshop: detours, salaries, regrets, all of it.

responses.label: Trade something back
responses.outcome: Their spreadsheets are a mess and your formatting is not. The mentorship becomes two way, which is what makes it last.

responses.label: Take notes, keep distance
responses.outcome: The advice lands even without the friendship. Thinner, and still nourishing.

cards.title: Different buses now
cards.body: Your Sec school best friend is in camp, or JC, or already earning. The rhythm that made you close is gone; the chat is down to birthday messages.

responses.label: Institutionalise the friendship
responses.outcome: First Sunday of the month, prata at Casuarina, no phones. Calendars beat sentiment at this age.

responses.label: Let it breathe
responses.outcome: Real ones survive dormancy. Two years later the conversation resumes mid sentence, as if the bus had just been long.

responses.label: Say the honest thing
responses.outcome: I miss you and I am rubbish at this, you type. The reply takes nine minutes and fixes eight months.
responses.stretch: It reads needier than you meant. Sent anyway, it turns out need was the accurate word.

cards.title: It gets shared
cards.body: The thing you posted at midnight, the timelapse, the repair video, the cover, wakes up to four hundred shares and a DM from an account with a blue tick.

responses.label: Post the next one weekly
responses.outcome: Consistency, not virality, builds the following. By month six the DMs include two paid offers.

responses.label: Answer the blue tick
responses.outcome: It is a brand looking for cheap content, and a negotiation you have never done. You do it anyway, at a price you Googled.
responses.stretch: The first quote you send is embarrassingly low and they accept instantly. Tuition paid; lesson pricier.

responses.label: Enjoy it and log off
responses.outcome: Screenshots saved, ego fed, homework due. Not every spark needs to become a job.

cards.title: The call from home
cards.body: Grandpa falls in the kitchen. Suddenly your week has hospital visits, translated discharge summaries and a rota your parents cannot cover alone.

responses.label: Take the structured share
responses.outcome: Tuesday and Saturday are yours at the ward. The course flexes, the family holds, and you learn what you are made of.

responses.label: Tell the school early
responses.outcome: The year tutor extends two deadlines without ceremony. Institutions bend for students who ask before breaking.

responses.label: Absorb it silently
responses.outcome: Grades dip, nobody knows why, and the semester costs double. Some silences are expensive.

onwardMoves: Every campus has leave of absence and deadline extension processes built for exactly this.
The hospital medical social worker can arrange subsidised care within a fortnight.

cards.title: The wrong course feeling
cards.body: Week eight. The module everyone else loves bores you to tears, and the course you dismissed keeps appearing in your search history at 1am.

responses.label: Test it before jumping
responses.outcome: One cross faculty elective, one open lecture, two coffees with students inside it. The feeling survives contact, which means it is data.

responses.label: Use the transfer window
responses.outcome: Paperwork, one interview, one lost semester. Cheaper at eighteen than at thirty eight, by a decade.
responses.stretch: The transfer board asks why and your answer is still half formed. Forming it out loud is the actual application.

responses.label: Finish what you started
responses.outcome: The diploma completes; the itch waits. Plenty of people love their second field from the payroll of their first.

onwardMoves: Course transfer windows open twice yearly at poly and uni; the deadline is fixed.
An elective inside the other course costs nothing but a semester slot.

cards.title: The gig lands on exam week
cards.body: A real client wants the job done the same fortnight as finals: eight hundred dollars, a portfolio piece, and a sleep schedule that would frighten a doctor.

responses.label: Negotiate the timeline
responses.outcome: Can deliver the week after finals, you write, expecting to lose it. They reply: fine. Most deadlines are opening offers.

responses.label: Decline with a referral
responses.outcome: You pass it to a coursemate with a freer week. The client remembers the professionalism; the coursemate owes you one.

responses.label: Do both, barely
responses.outcome: Both survive, neither shines, and you learn your actual capacity by exceeding it once.

cards.title: Your body sends a bill
cards.body: The all nighters, the skipped meals, the training on an unstretched hamstring: something gives. A doctor uses the word overuse and the word rest, twice.

responses.label: Actually rest
responses.outcome: Three weeks of doing less, properly. The work waits; the body forgives; the habit of listening starts here.

responses.label: Redesign the week
responses.outcome: Sleep becomes a timetabled subject. Marks go up when the human maintaining them is maintained.

responses.label: Push through anyway
responses.outcome: The second visit costs more than the first. The body keeps honest books.

onwardMoves: Campus clinics are subsidised and physio referrals are routine.
Three restful weeks now beat three limping months later.

cards.title: Trusted early
cards.body: The supervisor is short handed and looks at you: can you run Saturday's session, or the client demo, or the closing shift, alone? You are the youngest by a decade.

responses.label: Say yes, prepare hard
responses.outcome: Friday night is checklists. Saturday runs clean, and the word reliable attaches itself to your name where you cannot see it.
responses.stretch: Two things go sideways and improvisation carries you. Roughly done is still done alone.

responses.label: Ask for a shadow first
responses.outcome: Once with backup, then solo. The ladder still gets climbed; the rungs stay under your feet.

responses.label: Pass this one
responses.outcome: Someone hungrier takes it and dines out on it. Appetite, this once, was the qualification.

cards.title: The GP essay bites back
cards.body: Your General Paper tutor reads your essay aloud, then asks the class to demolish it. Halfway through the demolition you realise you disagree, with reasons.

responses.label: Defend it on your feet
responses.outcome: Standing, voice cracking once, you rebuild the argument under fire. The tutor grins: now that is a thesis.
responses.stretch: Your defence wobbles and half collapses. Arguing a losing position aloud is the gym where conviction trains.

responses.label: Rewrite it stronger
responses.outcome: Draft two absorbs the demolition and comes back armoured. Criticism, metabolised, is protein.

cards.title: The scholarship question
cards.body: A teacher slides the form across: you should try for this. The bond clause is six years long and the interview panel eats undergraduates for breakfast.

responses.label: Apply with open eyes
responses.outcome: Bond years are real years, you tell the mirror, and apply anyway. The interview toughens you regardless of the letter.
responses.stretch: The panel finds the gap in your answers in four minutes. The rejection letter teaches; round two exists.

responses.label: Study the fine print first
responses.outcome: Two scholarship holders and one bond breaker later, you understand the trade fully. Whatever you sign now, you sign informed.

cards.title: The module goes live
cards.body: Your group's class project, the booking system, the campaign, the prototype, gets picked by the module's real client to actually use. With your names in the footer.

responses.label: Own the handover
responses.outcome: Documentation, training video, a bugs channel. The client's thank you email becomes page one of your portfolio.

responses.label: Fix it when it breaks
responses.outcome: Week three, production falls over at 9pm. Your group swarms it by 11. Breakage, handled, is the best reference.

cards.title: The uni arithmetic
cards.body: A talk in the LT lays it out: what a 3.6 GPA reaches, what SIT weighs, what SMU's accelerated pathway takes from poly. Rows of calculators come out.

responses.label: Plan backwards from a number
responses.outcome: The target GPA becomes semester by semester module maths on your wall. Abstract dreams enjoy being turned into arithmetic.

responses.label: Ask the admissions human
responses.outcome: The university officer at the booth answers the question the slides dodged. Portfolios, she says, move borderline cases.

cards.title: The foreman's read
cards.body: First week on site, the foreman watches you coil cable. Wrong, he says, once, and shows you. Then he watches whether you keep it when unwatched.

responses.label: Do it right unwatched
responses.outcome: He catches you doing it properly at 5pm on a Friday. Monday you get the tasks with actual learning inside them.

responses.label: Ask him why his way
responses.outcome: Because of what fails, he says, and shows you a burnt junction box. Twenty years of why, yours for the asking.

cards.title: The machine nobody touches
cards.body: The workshop's new CNC rig arrives with a manual in three languages and a lecturer who has not read any of them. It sits there, expensive and unloved.

responses.label: Become its person
responses.outcome: Manual, forum posts, two ruined offcuts. By August you are the one who inducts everyone, staff included.
responses.stretch: The first month is mostly error messages. Machines respect stubbornness; so, eventually, does the lecturer.

responses.label: Learn it beside someone
responses.outcome: You and the quiet classmate split the manual. Half the glory, twice the speed, one lasting ally.

cards.title: Money for the work
cards.body: A hawker stall two blocks down wants a mural: two hundred dollars, your design, their wall, their aunties supervising with opinions.

responses.label: Take it, contract and all
responses.outcome: Deposit, sketch approval, two weekends of painting while the laksa aunties direct. The wall outlives everything else you made this year.

responses.label: Counter with your real rate
responses.outcome: Four hundred, you say, voice steady, portfolio open. They settle at three, and the number resets your sense of worth.
responses.stretch: They laugh you down to two fifty. Naming a price aloud, and surviving the laugh, is the actual commission.

cards.title: Can eat or not?
cards.body: Your uncle, kindly, over dinner: art ah? Can eat or not? Your mother's silence does more asking than he does.

responses.label: Answer with numbers
responses.outcome: Freelance rates, teaching gigs, the design studio salary bands. Feelings do not persuade uncles; spreadsheets sometimes do.

responses.label: Show them the invoice
responses.outcome: The zine table money and the mural deposit sit in your bank statement. Can eat, you say. Modestly, so far.

responses.label: Give it time to answer
responses.outcome: You change the subject and let the decade argue for you. Some cases are won by outliving the jury.

cards.title: The vocation letter
cards.body: PES result, then the posting: not the vocation you typed into the wishlist. Someone in the bunk got yours, and he did not even want it.

responses.label: Master the one given
responses.outcome: Transport, signals, medic, whatever it says: you decide to be excellent at it. Excellence turns out to be portable.

responses.label: Appeal it properly
responses.outcome: The paperwork route exists and you take it: letter, interview, wait. It fails, mostly, and teaches you how appeals work everywhere.

responses.label: Trade knowledge anyway
responses.outcome: The bunkmate with your dream vocation teaches you his manuals at night. The army posted the body; the learning went where you sent it.

cards.title: The command school letter
cards.body: Your sergeant recommends you for command school. Longer days, heavier bag, and a version of you that gives orders you used to dodge.

responses.label: Take the course
responses.outcome: Leading tired strangers politely at 4am is the hardest soft skill on earth. Employers never stop asking about it.
responses.stretch: You scrape through middle of the cohort. Scraping through command school still means you commanded.

responses.label: Decline, master your post
responses.outcome: Not every ladder needs climbing. You become the specialist the officers quietly depend on instead.

cards.title: The bunk teaches
cards.body: Twelve men, four school systems, one ceiling fan. The ITE grad rewires the illegal kettle; the JC boy drafts everyone's appeal letters; you learn to fall asleep to two languages.

responses.label: Collect their maps
responses.outcome: By ORD you understand poly GPA, JC rank points and site pay rates equally. Nobody leaves with a wider map than yours.

responses.label: Teach your piece
responses.outcome: Your subject, whatever it was, becomes the bunk's tutorial on guard duty nights. Teaching cements it into you permanently.

cards.title: The ankle goes
cards.body: Route march, uneven ground, a pop you hear before you feel. MC, crutches, downgrade review, and the platoon moving on without your rifle.

responses.label: Rehab like a job
responses.outcome: Physio exercises done at double the prescribed diligence. The ankle returns; the discipline it taught outstays it.

responses.label: Fill the desk months
responses.outcome: Excused duties come with desk time. You finish an online cert the platoon has no idea exists.

responses.label: Sink a while, then swim
responses.outcome: Watching your section pass out without you stings for weeks. Recovery has a morale curve, and it bends up.

onwardMoves: Military physio and downgrade reviews are systematic; work the system.
Desk postings finish more certificates than anyone admits.

cards.title: Forty eight hour weekends
cards.body: Book out Friday 6pm, book in Sunday 9pm. The bunk splits into those who sleep the window and those who build something inside it.

responses.label: Study the window
responses.outcome: Driving licence, an online module, uni application essays drafted in the camp library. ORD arrives with paper in hand.

responses.label: Bank the window
responses.outcome: Every book out costs less than the bunk thinks is possible. You ORD with four figures and first month's freedom.

responses.label: Live the window
responses.outcome: Family dinners, the girlfriend, the football. The service takes two years; it does not get the weekends too.

cards.title: The month after ORD
cards.body: Pink IC back, hair growing out, and a strange month where nobody tells you where to stand. Course starts in August; it is April.

responses.label: Work the gap
responses.outcome: Three months of logistics temp work at Changi. Money banked, and an answer for every interviewer who asks about the gap.

responses.label: Travel it cheap
responses.outcome: Trains through Malaysia with two bunkmates and a shoestring. The photos age better than the savings would have.

responses.label: Rest it, honestly
responses.outcome: Two years of 5am wants paying back. You sleep, read and reset, and start the course actually hungry.

cards.title: While they serve
cards.body: Half your Sec school group chat is in camouflage green. You are in week three of your course, and someone types: study for us also ah.

responses.label: Carry the flag
responses.outcome: Their book out suppers become your progress reports both ways. The head start is real; you spend it well and share the notes.

responses.label: Visit the camp gate
responses.outcome: Passing food over the fence at Pasir Laba teaches you what the two years actually cost. The friendship deepens oddly.

cards.title: Youngest in the room
cards.body: Everyone else in the internship intake is post NS and two years older. The supervisor keeps calling you the baby, fondly, while giving you the boring tickets.

responses.label: Outdeliver the label
responses.outcome: Boring tickets, done immaculately and early, become interesting tickets by month two. Age stops being the headline.

responses.label: Borrow their two years
responses.outcome: The older interns explain rent, bosses and one bad tattoo decision. Their detours become your shortcuts.

cards.title: The management question
cards.body: The director asks whether you want the team lead post. More pay, no more making, and every problem arriving pre argued by two colleagues.

responses.label: Take it and learn people
responses.outcome: The first year of managing is remedial empathy at speed. Some days you miss the craft; most days you multiply it.

responses.label: Decline, name your lane
responses.outcome: I am better used deep, you say, and mean it. The org, surprisingly, respects a person with a defined edge.

responses.label: Ask for the hybrid
responses.outcome: Half a team, half the craft. Rarely offered, sometimes granted to the person who thinks to ask.

cards.title: The restructure email
cards.body: All hands meeting at 4pm, calendar invite with no agenda. By 4:20 your department has a new name and eleven fewer people, and one of them is you.

responses.label: Work the system same week
responses.outcome: WSG career coach booked, resume rewritten, e2i fair attended, severance banked. Process is what dignity looks like in week one.

responses.label: Take the bridge job
responses.outcome: Three months of contract work steadies the mortgage while the real search runs. Momentum beats moping arithmetic.

responses.label: Retrain toward the gap
responses.outcome: The SkillsFuture course list gets read like a menu for once. Mid career conversion programmes exist precisely for this Tuesday.

onwardMoves: Workforce Singapore assigns career coaches free within two weeks.
Career conversion programmes pay salary support while you retrain.
Severance plus two calm months beats one panicked signature.

cards.title: The tool does your Tuesday
cards.body: The new AI tooling drafts in seconds what used to be your Tuesday. Management calls it augmentation. The intern calls it normal.

responses.label: Get ahead of it
responses.outcome: Three months of deliberate practice later, you supervise the tool instead of racing it. The job moves up a floor.

responses.label: Double down on the human bits
responses.outcome: Judgement, site presence, the client's trust: you concentrate where the tool cannot follow. The mix stabilises.

responses.label: Ride it out grumbling
responses.outcome: Two years of quiet resistance later the floor moves anyway. Late is more expensive than early.

onwardMoves: Employer funded upskilling exists this quarter; ask before the next reorg.
The colleagues who learned the tool first are teaching it now.

cards.title: The flat spreadsheet
cards.body: BTO or resale, grants, the CPF numbers, a queue number that feels like a lottery. The spreadsheet has two names on it, or one, and either is fine.

responses.label: Buy within one salary
responses.outcome: The conservative sum wins: a flat one person can carry alone. Every career risk after this is cheaper because of it.

responses.label: Stretch for the location
responses.outcome: Nearer the parents, nearer the MRT, heavier mortgage. Some prices buy time, and time is the scarce one now.

responses.label: Wait another cycle
responses.outcome: Renting near work for two more years keeps you liquid for the pivot you can feel coming.

cards.title: The diagnosis
cards.body: Your father's scan comes back with a word on it. The doctor talks to you, not him, because you are the one taking notes now.

responses.label: Build the care system
responses.outcome: Roster, helper application, subsidy forms, one family meeting with an agenda. Grief postponed by administration, then felt properly.

responses.label: Downshift a gear openly
responses.outcome: Your boss hears it straight: eighteen months of ninety percent. The career pauses; it does not break.

responses.label: Split it with siblings
responses.outcome: The rota shares the load and redistributes old resentments. Families renegotiate under pressure, mostly upward.

onwardMoves: The medical social worker at every public hospital unlocks subsidies in one meeting.
Caregiver leave and flexible work requests have legal standing now.
The Agency for Integrated Care coordinates home support within weeks.

cards.title: The shelved thing knocks
cards.body: Clearing a drawer you find it: the sketchbook, the business plan, the half built kit. The person who shelved it had reasons. Some of them have expired.

responses.label: Give it Tuesday nights
responses.outcome: Two hours a week, no stakes, no audience. Six months later it is undeniably alive again, and so is a piece of you.

responses.label: Fund it a real course
responses.outcome: The SkillsFuture balance finally gets spent on the thing you actually wanted. The classroom is full of your kind of people.

responses.label: Close the drawer kindly
responses.outcome: Not every want survives its winter, and that is allowed. You keep the sketchbook and the peace.

cards.title: The junior asks you
cards.body: The new hire, twenty two and terrified, asks how you got here. You open your mouth to give the tidy version and stop.

responses.label: Tell the true version
responses.outcome: Detours, the failed first job, the course you nearly quit. Their shoulders drop an inch. Honesty is senior work.

responses.label: Show them one real move
responses.outcome: Instead of the story you give them one door: the cert that mattered, the person to ask. Maps beat memoirs.

cards.title: The plateau years
cards.body: Three years, same title, same number after the dollar sign. LinkedIn keeps showing you a classmate's promotion announcements with balloons on them.

responses.label: Price yourself outside
responses.outcome: Two external interviews later you know your market number. You take it back inside, or out the door, but informed either way.

responses.label: Grow sideways on purpose
responses.outcome: The adjacent skill, the cross team project, the certification: width now buys height later. Plateaus are load bearing.

responses.label: Mute the balloons
responses.outcome: Comparison is a subscription you cancel. The classmate's ladder was never pointed where yours goes.

onwardMoves: A market interview costs one afternoon and reprices your confidence.
Internal transfers move more careers than resignations do.

cards.title: Twenty years later, one table
cards.body: Class reunion at a tze char place. The ITE guy owns two shops; the JC scholar just quit law happily; the quiet one became the nurse everyone calls first.

responses.label: Compare maps openly
responses.outcome: Four roads, one table, nobody's straight. The form you all filled at fourteen decided the first step and almost nothing else.

responses.label: Recruit shamelessly
responses.outcome: The shop owner needs exactly what you do. Old classmates skip three interviews' worth of trust.

cards.title: The second wind window
cards.body: The career conversion programme takes people your age into the field you almost chose at seventeen. Salary support included, ego support not.

responses.label: Apply, age and all
responses.outcome: Oldest in the cohort by a decade, and the fastest through the practicum. Twenty years of adjacent skill was not nothing.
responses.stretch: Being taught by someone your junior stings for a fortnight, then stops mattering. The field was worth the swallow.

responses.label: Take the evening version
responses.outcome: Part time, twenty months, employed throughout. Slower, safer, same destination and the mortgage never noticed.

cards.title: The Year Head's list, done
cards.body: Subject review week. Two years ago you asked the Year Head what moving up takes; her checklist has lived in your phone since. Every box on it is ticked.

responses.label: Table it at the review
responses.outcome: The meeting is short: evidence beats pleading. The recommendation goes in with her signature attached.

responses.label: Pass the list down
responses.outcome: A Sec 1 asks how moving up works. You forward the checklist with your own ticks as proof it is real.

cards.title: She remembers you asked
cards.body: EAE season. The teacher you asked about moving up two years ago hears, finds you at the canteen, and offers to write the reference herself.

responses.label: Accept, and draft with her
responses.outcome: Two lunchtimes of drafting later the reference reads like a case, not a compliment. Asking early, it turns out, compounds.

responses.label: Ask her one more thing
responses.outcome: While she has the pen out: what would you study, if you were me? Her answer rearranges your shortlist.

cards.title: The folder was ready
cards.body: EAE interview, and the panel asks for evidence. Your folder from Sec 3 opens: the project, the screenshots, the write up, already there.

responses.label: Walk them through it
responses.outcome: Ten minutes of show, not tell. One panellist writes something and underlines it twice.

responses.label: Leave it with them
responses.outcome: The folder speaks after you leave the room, which is what folders are for.

cards.title: The scrap paper ladder
cards.body: Clearing your wallet you find it: the ladder the ECG officer drew, 2.5 applies, 3.5 guarantees. You are standing on the exact rung she pointed at.

responses.label: Send her the photo
responses.outcome: Made it to the rung, you type. Teachers keep these messages in a folder for their bad days; she tells you so.

responses.label: Draw the next ladder
responses.outcome: Same paper, next five years, your own handwriting this time. The habit of mapping was the real gift.

cards.title: Your mother, at the wedding
cards.body: A relative starts the old song about your path. Across the table your mother, who you once braced to disappoint, cuts in with your exact reasoning. Word for word.

responses.label: Catch her eye
responses.outcome: The smallest nod passes between you. Telling them early, it turns out, recruited them.

responses.label: Add the update
responses.outcome: And since then, you say, and list what has moved. The relative changes subject to property prices.

cards.title: The clinic remembers
cards.body: The place you shadowed at fifteen emails: holiday relief role, paid, start Monday. The nurse manager wrote one line: ask the one who asked good questions.

responses.label: Take the fortnight
responses.outcome: Two weeks of real shifts. The reference letter afterwards names specifics, which is the only kind that works.

responses.label: Refer your classmate too
responses.outcome: You bring the coursemate who needs it more, and split the shifts. The manager notes that as well.

cards.title: The DSA thread pays out
cards.body: Because you asked about DSA early, you know the timeline cold. Your teammate does not, and the window shuts in nine days.

responses.label: Walk her through the portal
responses.outcome: Her application lands with a day to spare. She gets the offer; you get the strange rich feeling of an assist.

responses.label: Compare your options aloud
responses.outcome: Talking her through it clarifies your own: you apply too, eyes open about the binding bit.

cards.title: The comma number
cards.body: The internship company calls two months before you graduate. The team lead kept your number, as promised. The offer has a comma in it.

responses.label: Negotiate anyway
responses.outcome: Even a good first offer respects a counter. Two hundred more and a training budget, for one brave email.
responses.stretch: The counter comes out apologetic and they hold firm. The asking muscle, once found, keeps.

responses.label: Accept and start strong
responses.outcome: First day, the standup nods at you like a returning cast member. Continuity is a salary of its own.

cards.title: The two time zone chat
cards.body: The exchange semester group chat wakes up: the Rotterdam flatmate's company is opening a Singapore office and she typed your name first.

responses.label: Take the interview
responses.outcome: Half interview, half reunion. The offer letter cites international experience, which is chat speak for you already know her.

responses.label: Trade the intro onward
responses.outcome: Wrong fit for you, perfect for your colleague. Brokering it costs nothing and mints trust on both sides.

cards.title: The mentor's sentence
cards.body: A job you want, a shortlist you are not on. Then the hiring manager mentions your mentor's name, and one sentence from that quarter moves your CV to the top.

responses.label: Deliver on the vouch
responses.outcome: You over prepare and arrive early for a year. Vouches are loans; repayment is performance.

responses.label: Thank them properly
responses.outcome: Kopi, in person, and the story of what their sentence did. Mentors run on exactly this fuel.

cards.title: The form teacher was right
cards.body: Mid Sec 3, the subject your form teacher steered you toward is the one you stopped watching the clock in. You almost took the other one for the friend group.

responses.label: Tell her it landed
responses.outcome: Teachers plant forests they rarely see. You show her one tree, and her whole week visibly improves.

responses.label: Apply the method again
responses.outcome: How you learn turned out to matter more than what sounds impressive. You reuse that lens on every choice after.

cards.title: The senior's warning
cards.body: Week one of the course, and the exact trap the senior described appears on schedule: the module everyone fails by underestimating week three.

responses.label: Front load week three
responses.outcome: Forewarned, you bank the hard module early while classmates discover it the expensive way. One teh, repaid tenfold.

responses.label: Pass the warning down
responses.outcome: You type the same warning into the freshie chat the senior once typed to you. The chain letter of survival continues.

cards.title: You have walked this corridor
cards.body: First day of the course, and the corridor is familiar: you stood here at the open house, asking the second year about workload. Now someone is asking you.

responses.label: Answer like they answered
responses.outcome: Honest numbers, no brochure voice. The freshie exhales the way you once did.

responses.label: Find that second year
responses.outcome: They are final year now. The thank you turns into a coffee, the coffee into your first senior ally.

cards.title: The bazaar, but bigger
cards.body: The teacher running Open House needs a logistics IC and asks the one who caught the toppling bazaar. Two hundred visitors this time, and a budget.

responses.label: Run it with a system
responses.outcome: Spreadsheets, walkie talkies, two near disasters caught early. Your EAE folder gains its centrepiece story.

responses.label: Co lead and delegate
responses.outcome: You take half and hand half to the Sec 2 you are training. Leadership, it turns out, is mostly succession.

cards.title: The cousin's map
cards.body: The family member who took the different road calls back: an open day at her workplace, your name already on the visitor list.

responses.label: Go and shadow her
responses.outcome: A day inside her actual Tuesday rewrites your guesses about the field. Family opens doors brochures cannot.

responses.label: Bring your questions list
responses.outcome: Pay, hours, the boring parts: she answers what no website will. Blood plus honesty equals data.

cards.title: The lecturer's one line
cards.body: Applying onward, you ask the lecturer whose road you once asked about. The recommendation arrives same week, with a line only someone who knows you could write.

responses.label: Build on the specific
responses.outcome: The line names your debugging patience. You lead with exactly that in the interview, and it lands.

responses.label: Keep the relationship warm
responses.outcome: A thank you, then an update every semester. References age well when watered.

cards.title: The careers office remembers
cards.body: The career centre you actually used sends a targeted ping: an employer asked for someone exactly like your profile, interview slots this Thursday.

responses.label: Take the Thursday slot
responses.outcome: Prepped by the same office that flagged you, the interview feels rigged in your favour. It half was.

responses.label: Forward it to a friend
responses.outcome: Wrong city for you, right everything for him. The office notes that you multiply their work.

cards.title: The promotion map, used
cards.body: Eighteen months after you asked what promotion takes, you hand your supervisor the completed list. She checks it twice, then starts the paperwork.

responses.label: Bank it and set the next
responses.outcome: Title, increment, and the same question asked again for the next rung. Ladders yield to people with checklists.

responses.label: Ask for scope, not title
responses.outcome: Instead of the name change you take the project with your name on the outcome. Titles follow scope, eventually.

cards.title: The borrowed blueprint
cards.body: The friend whose life you once asked about calls: she is reorganising again, and wants your eyes on it this time. The blueprint borrowing has become mutual.

responses.label: Trade honest audits
responses.outcome: Two afternoons, two lives on the table, no varnish. You each leave with one change worth making.

responses.label: Adopt her next move
responses.outcome: Her four day week experiment becomes your proposal at work. Proven elsewhere is the strongest argument.

cards.title: The reverse lesson sticks
cards.body: The junior you asked to teach you the new tool now runs a team, and tells the story of the senior who asked, as the reason she asks juniors herself.

responses.label: Keep the habit visible
responses.outcome: You ask the next junior about the next tool, in the open plan, on purpose. Culture is just repeated behaviour with witnesses.

responses.label: Formalise the exchange
responses.outcome: Reverse mentoring becomes an actual programme with your name on the proposal. HR loves it; the interns rate it.

cards.title: The kitchen table council
cards.body: Because home already knows what you are weighing, the decision gets a council: your partner with the spreadsheet, your mother with the question nobody else dares ask.

responses.label: Let them stress test it
responses.outcome: The plan that survives your mother's questioning survives anything. You proceed, reinforced.

responses.label: Delegate one piece each
responses.outcome: The spreadsheet, the school run maths, the what if column: shared out, the weight halves.

cards.title: The side thing gets found
cards.body: Someone you respect finds the thing you built on the side and asks the question every maker waits for: is this yours?

responses.label: Own it fully
responses.outcome: Yes, you say, and the conversation becomes an opportunity wearing casual clothes. Made things are self introducing.

responses.label: Show the process too
responses.outcome: The messy folder of drafts interests them more than the polished result. Process is the proof of the next one.

cards.title: The client wants more
cards.body: The small paying gig from before sends a bigger brief: triple the scope, a real deadline, and the sentence we trust you with this.

responses.label: Price it properly this time
responses.outcome: Scope, timeline, half upfront. The client signs without blinking, and your rate resets permanently.
responses.stretch: The quote takes three drafts and a pep talk. Sending it is the skill; the number was secondary.

responses.label: Grow it with a partner
responses.outcome: Half the fee, half the panic, twice the capacity. The collaboration outlasts the brief.

cards.title: The one you helped
cards.body: The classmate you once sat with, the one everyone gave up on, appears in your DMs: qualified, employed, and hiring for a junior role. You first, they typed.

responses.label: Take the interview
responses.outcome: The loop closes: kindness at fourteen, shortlisted at twenty something. Nobody designs these returns; they just compound.

responses.label: Send them someone
responses.outcome: You are settled, but your junior is not. The kindness forwards itself, with your name in the chain.

cards.title: They remember the stage
cards.body: Speech day needs an emcee and the teacher in charge remembers you from the stage, the pitch, the heats. The script is thin and the hall seats nine hundred.

responses.label: Take the mic
responses.outcome: Two rehearsals, one wardrobe crisis, zero disasters. Nine hundred people now file you under confident, inaccurately, usefully.
responses.stretch: Your voice shakes for the first minute, then finds the floor. Nobody remembers minute one; you remember minute nine.

responses.label: Co host with a junior
responses.outcome: You split the script with a Sec 2 who needs the rep. The teacher notes the generosity in her little book.

cards.title: The door back opens
cards.body: Two years into work with your Nitec, the boss asks if you want the part time Higher Nitec, company sponsored. Mr Rashid said the door would stay open. It did.

responses.label: Take the sponsored seat
responses.outcome: Evenings at ITE, days on site, certificate in twenty months. The route back was real, and paid for.

responses.label: Counter with work study
responses.outcome: The SkillsFuture work study version pays better and maps the same. You bring the brochure to the boss.

cards.title: The GPA clears the bar
cards.body: Poly application results. The Year 3 you stayed for produced the GPA, and the GPA produced this: an offer letter with your first choice course on it.

responses.label: Accept and thank the workshop
responses.outcome: You send Mr Rashid the screenshot. Knew it, he replies, with a spanner emoji.

responses.label: Defer for the savings year
responses.outcome: Offer accepted, start deferred, one year of full time pay banked first. The letter keeps; the plan compounds.

cards.title: Ms D asks back
cards.body: The teacher whose two circled habits fixed your paper stops you: she is trialling a peer coaching scheme and wants you as the first tutor.

responses.label: Take the Tuesday slot
responses.outcome: Teaching the two habits to Sec 2s cements them in you permanently. The scheme grows; so does your reference letter.

responses.label: Suggest a better fit
responses.outcome: You know the classmate who explains things even better. Ms D takes you both.

cards.title: Plan B, pre installed
cards.body: The main plan wobbles: the cut off moves, the intake shrinks. Around you, panic. In your notes app, the alternative you researched months ago, with its deadline still open.

responses.label: Execute the researched turn
responses.outcome: The pivot takes one evening because the homework predates the emergency. Calm is mostly preparation wearing a nice shirt.

responses.label: Share the doc
responses.outcome: Your comparison table circulates the group chat within the hour. Half a cohort borrows your homework, gratefully.
